jobs.description:
Division:  IGM Technology

Location:  Toronto/Winnipeg

IGM Financial Inc. is a leading wealth and asset management company in Canada, managing approximately $310 billion in assets as of December 31, 2025. It offers financial planning and investment services to over two million Canadians through IG Wealth Management and Mackenzie Investments.

Founded in 1926, IG Wealth Management is a key part of IGM's business model, providing comprehensive wealth management services to Canadian financial advisors and their clients.

With a vision to inspire financial confidence, IG Wealth Management is recognized as one of Manitoba’s Top Employers, Canada’s Top 100 Employers, and Best Diversity Employers, aiming to innovate the industry and support Canadians in achieving their financial goals.

Join our team to engage in continuous learning and skill development in a supportive environment. Experience the best of both worlds with our hybrid work environment, where you spend three days a week in the office, connecting, collaborating, and enjoying quality time with your amazing colleagues! Our Values: Be better; we strive for improvement in everything we do. Be accountable; we foster clarity and are empowered to act responsibly. Be a team; we are united to drive collective impact to achieve our goals.

Overall Job Purpose

The Director, Citizen Development & Employee Technology Experience Pod Owner is responsible for leading and advancing two connected enterprise capabilities: enabling employees to safely improve how work gets done through Microsoft Copilot, Power Automate and approved low-code/no-code capabilities; and reducing technology friction through stronger employee experiences, communications, onboarding, short-form learning, TechTalks and adoption programs.

This role shapes and delivers the pod strategy, roadmap, operating model, governance, prioritization and measurable outcomes. The Director balances speed, innovation and employee empowerment with security, privacy, risk, operational resilience and supportability, ensuring employee-led technology adoption remains practical, governed and sustainable.

Key Accountabilities

Lead the pod vision, strategy, roadmap and priorities for Citizen Development and Employee Technology Experience, ensuring alignment to enterprise objectives, portfolio priorities and measurable business outcomes.
Operate and launch and then continuously improve the Citizen Development operating model, including scope, intake, prioritization, decision rights, solution classification, lifecycle oversight, support model, escalation paths and value measurement.
Enable governed adoption of Microsoft Copilot, Power Automate and approved low-code/no-code capabilities, with clear boundaries between employee-led solutions and work requiring business-led or technology-led delivery.
Maintain practical guardrails for safe innovation, including solution registration, ownership, risk tiering, control gates, security review, privacy considerations and operational supportability.
Identify employee technology friction across corporate and advisor communities and sponsor practical improvements that improve productivity, adoption, service experience and confidence in technology.
Lead employee technology communications, TechTalks, digital learning content, short video learning, tech tips, onboarding support and awareness campaigns that make technology easier to understand and adopt.
Manage and refine the pod backlog, making informed trade-offs across value, risk, cost, capacity, quality, employee experience, technical sustainability and operational impact.
Coordinate agile planning, backlog refinement, sprint execution, reviews and retrospectives to maintain delivery discipline, transparency and momentum.
Provide day-to-day leadership, coaching and feedback to pod team members; partner with Product and Delivery Chapters on standards, capability development, staffing and best practices.
Build strong partnerships across business teams, Technology, Security, Risk, Privacy, Architecture, Service Management, enterprise platform teams and corporate support functions.
Communicate roadmaps, progress, risks, decisions, dependencies and performance clearly to stakeholders and senior leaders.
Track measures for adoption, employee experience, productivity, business value, cost, operational health, risk and supportability, and use insights to improve priorities and outcomes.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Technology, Digital Transformation or a related field required; equivalent experience considered an asset
5–8 years of progressive experience in enterprise technology, digital workplace, product, automation, artificial intelligence, employee experience, service management or technology delivery
Experience supporting strategies, operating models, roadmaps, governance frameworks and measurable outcomes for enterprise technology capabilities
Knowledge of Microsoft 365, Microsoft Copilot, Power Platform, Power Automate and related enterprise technology environments
Strong understanding of governance, security, privacy, technology risk, operational resilience and support models in a regulated environment
Ability to translate emerging technology into practical employee and business value
Strong communication, influencing, stakeholder-management and decision-framing skills
Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary work, manage priorities and coordinate delivery across organizational boundaries
Collaborative, pragmatic, change-oriented and outcome-focused leadership style
Passion for improving employee technology experience, reducing friction and enabling safe, governed innovation

What Success Looks Like

Success means employees can confidently adopt technology and safely improve how work gets done; technology friction is visible and addressed; Citizen Development operates within clear boundaries and guardrails; and leaders have reliable visibility into adoption, employee experience, business value, cost, operational health and risk.

The expected annual base salary range for this role is $149,500 - $192,500 which is determined based on skills, knowledge and experience and geographic location. In addition to base salary, this role is eligible for annual short-term incentive, health and well-being benefits, retirement and savings plan, paid time off and career development.

Benefits

COMPETITIVE COMPENSATION & RECOGNITION: competitive base salary, performance-weighted bonus, education/career support, option to join Employee Share Purchase Plan with employer matching component.
EMPLOYEE BENEFITS & INSURANCE: competitive health and dental coverage, flexible plan for you and your family and short-term & long-term disability plans.
RETIREMENT SAVINGS PROGRAMS: voluntary Defined Contribution Pension Plan
WORK LIFE BALANCE: paid volunteer days, competitive time off, including 10 wellness days off, WorkPerks discount program, hybrid & flex work arrangements.
INCLUSIVE CULTURE AND DIVERSITY: living our core values: Be a Team, Be Accountable, Be Better, engaging with community through Business Resource Groups (BRG communities are volunteer employee-led groups formed around a common interest, identity, or background).

IGM is a diverse workplace committed to doing business inclusively - this starts with having a representative workforce! We encourage applications from all qualified candidates that represent the diversity present across Canada – including racialized persons, women, Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+ community, gender diverse and neurodiverse individuals, as well as all who may contribute to the further diversification of ideas.

IG is an accessible employer committed to providing a barrier- free recruitment experience. If you require an accommodation or this information in an alternate format at any stage of the recruitment process, please reach out to the Talent Acquisition team who will work with you to meet your needs.

How to Apply: Interested candidates are invited to submit their resume and a cover letter detailing their qualifications and experience to https://www.ig.ca/en/careers

We thank all applicants for their interest in IG Wealth Management; however, only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

Please apply before November 12 2026.

jobs.description:
About Toronto Community Housing Corporation

Toronto Community Housing Corporation (“TCHC”) is the largest social housing provider in Canada and the second largest in North America. We are wholly owned by the City of Toronto and operate in a non-profit manner. TCHC provides homes to over 41,000 low and moderate-income households in 88 of Toronto's neighbourhoods, with 93,000 tenants from many different backgrounds with a diversity in age, education, language, mental and physical ability, religion, ethnicity and race. We are an essential part of the City of Toronto's fabric and social system.

Our over 2,000 employees work to achieve our vision of quality homes in vibrant communities where people are proud to live and work.

Vacancy Type

Full-time Permanent

Salary Range

$165,001.67 - $198,002.01

Work Details (Days/Hours)

Monday – Friday, 36.25 hours per week

Hybrid Eligible

Yes

Affiliation

Non-Union: Management/Exempt

Division and Department

CEO Office

Number Of Vacancies

1

Existing/New Job

New

Grade

10

Vacancy Status

Existing Vacancy

Candidate List Or Eligibility List

Candidate List

What We Offer

In addition to competitive compensation and a rewarding career where you can truly make a difference, we offer a comprehensive package that meets the various needs of our diverse employees, including:

Ability to participate in inclusive employee-led networks to educate, inspire, amplify voices, build relationships and provide development opportunities;
Minimum four (4) weeks of paid annual vacation days, increasing with years of service;
Four (4) paid personal days;
Defined benefit pension plan with OMERS, includes 100-per-cent employer matching;
Health and dental benefits, including a health spending account available upon your start date;
Employee and family assistance program;
Maternity and parental leave top up (93% of base salary);
Training and development programs including tuition reimbursement of $1500 per calendar year;
Fitness membership discount.

Work location:
This job offers the opportunity to work from home as part of a hybrid work arrangement. This arrangement will allow you to work some days at a TCHC work location (Metro Hall – 55 John Street and/or 729 Petrolia Road) and the rest of the time from home. The amount of time required to work at a TCHC work location is flexible, while considering operational and service delivery requirements.

Make a difference

As the Director, Corporate Compliance and Enterprise Risk, you have a unique opportunity to build and operate TCHC’s corporate compliance function while shaping the future of enterprise risk management. Reporting directly to the President & CEO, you will develop practical frameworks, tools, and reporting that enable leaders to identify, assess and manage significant risks and compliance obligations.

As a trusted advisor to leaders across TCHC and to the Board of Directors, you will bring clarity to complex and emerging risks and inform enterprise-wide decisions. Your advice will strengthen transparency and accountability while ensuring leaders remain responsible for their processes, risks, controls, and corrective actions.

Through coaching, facilitation and fit-for-purpose solutions, you will build risk and compliance capability across TCHC, helping TCHC make informed decisions and ultimately deliver better outcomes for tenants and communities.

What You’ll Do

Corporate Compliance

Design, establish and operate a corporate compliance model that enables divisions to identify and manage legislative, regulatory, shareholder, funding, policy and other obligations.
Develop practical compliance tools, guidance, learning resources and reporting that business units can apply within day-to-day operations.
Partner with compliance owners to clarify obligations, assess exposure, address capability gaps and develop proportionate improvement plans.
Monitor changing requirements, coordinate enterprise-level compliance insights, and support escalation of significant compliance matters.

Enterprise Risk Management (ERM)

Shape and operate TCHC’s existing enterprise risk management model, including common risk language, assessment practices, risk appetite and tolerance, the enterprise risk profile and reporting cycle.
Facilitate enterprise and cross-divisional risk identification, assessment, prioritization and response planning with executives, risk owners and subject-matter leaders.
Support risk owners in developing proportionate responses, indicators and monitoring approaches, while ownership of risks, business processes and actions remains with management.
Integrate internal controls as one component of ERM by advising leaders on controls that support the treatment of priority risks and by helping them evaluate whether those controls remain fit for purpose.

Risk Advisory and Capacity Building

Provide concise, risk-based advice on the enterprise risk profile, significant compliance obligations and emerging risks.
Prepare and present integrated compliance and ERM reporting that supports executive and Board discussion, direction, and oversight while distinguishing management-owned corrective actions.
Support appropriate escalation of significant risk or compliance matters and track management commitments for executive and Board visibility.
Coach executives, leaders, risk owners and staff in risk-informed decision-making and compliance management.
Build sustainable capability through workshops, training, templates, communities of practice and decision supports.
Lead, coach and develop team, setting priorities and quality expectations.

What You’ll Need

An undergraduate degree in Risk Management, Business Administration, Public Administration, Law, Compliance, Finance or related discipline.
A recognized professional designation in enterprise risk management or compliance designation, such as CRM, CRMA, RIMS-CRMP, an IRM qualification, or CCEP (Certified Compliance & Ethics Professional) from the Society of Corporate Compliance and Ethics (SCCE), or an equivalent credential.
Minimum of 10 years of progressive senior experience establishing and operating complex enterprise risk management and corporate compliance functions, including experience designing practical frameworks, advising executives and Boards, leading professional teams, and building organizational capability in an organization of similar size and complexity.
Demonstrated success implementing or maturing compliance programs and ERM in a large public-sector, housing, non-profit or similarly regulated, complex and multi-stakeholder organization.
Expert knowledge of corporate compliance and ERM frameworks and practices, including COSO ERM, ISO 31000, ISO 37301.
Proven ability to translate risk and compliance principles into practical operating models, decision tools, reporting and coaching for business leaders.
Strong understanding of public-sector accountability, Board governance, shareholder and funding obligations, and risk-based reporting applicable to a large social housing provider.
Excellent strategic judgment, facilitation, relationship-building, coaching, change leadership and communication skills
Effective verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to present complex risk and compliance matters as clear options and advice.

What’s Next

Once you apply, we’ll review your resume and contact you if we believe your skills and experience will make you successful in the role. If you are selected to move forward, the process will include one or more interviews and/or assessments and reference checks.

INDS

Thank you for your interest in Toronto Community Housing

We recognize that people bring experience and talent that goes beyond the technical skills and requirements of a job. If you possess similar experience that is close to what we’ve included in the job postings below, we encourage you to consider applying. We strongly believe that diverse experience, transferable skills, and passion are key!

Once you have submitted your application successfully, you will receive a confirmation email. We encourage you to check out our careers page often, as new opportunities become available on a regular basis.

Our commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion

We are committed to providing equal opportunity to all employees and strive to create a diverse workplace that reflects the cultural mosaic of our great city and the communities we serve. We recognize the value that comes from different viewpoints, unique experiences and diverse perspectives of our employees, who bring fresh, new ideas to our business. Diversity plays a key role in our ability to deliver on our mission to provide clean, safe, well-maintained, affordable homes for tenants.

TCHC is committed to diversity and inclusion within its community and encourages applications from Indigenous peoples, racialized persons/persons of colour, persons with disabilities, women, 2SLGBTQ+ persons, and others who can help us provide vibrant communities and make our city a great place to live. In an effort to ensure access to information for people with disabilities, we have noticed that some screen readers do not function properly with our job portal. If you are a person with a disability and are experiencing issues with our job portal and would like access to our job postings in an alternative format, please email your request to our People and Culture Division at accessibility.hr@torontohousing.ca.

Accessibility for applicants

Toronto Community Housing is committed to equity in employment. Our goal is a diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free workplace that reflects the communities we serve.

We will provide reasonable accommodation to applicants with disabilities at all stages of the hiring process in accordance with the Ontario Human Rights Code, the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, 2005, and Toronto Community Housing’s Accessibility Policy.

If you are a person with a disability and need the job posting in an alternative format or any other accessible accommodations during the hiring process, please email your request to our People & Culture department at Accessibility.HR@torontohousing.ca or call our accessible accommodations line at (416) 981 - 4119. Technical Director / AI Lead – Epic Fantasy Franchise (5% Net Profit Share Equity)

We are building the future of cinematic animation, and we need our Architect.

"Echoes of the Silent God" is a high-concept, dark fantasy animated series combining the brutal world-building of Game of Thrones with the hyper-fluid, physics-defying "Sakuga" fight sequences of Dragon Ball Z and Mortal Kombat. We are bypassing the traditional million-dollar studio bottleneck by deploying an elite, agile 5-man AI-assisted pipeline to produce 21-minute episodic micro-dramas for a massive global digital release.

As the Technical Director, you will hold the keys to the engine. You will design, optimize, and oversee the entire generative video pipeline, establishing character consistency (identity-locking) and stylistic coherence that leaves traditional studios scrambling to catch up.

The Role:
- Architect and maintain our advanced AI generation pipeline (ComfyUI, custom local/cloud nodes).
- Train, fine-tune, and implement custom LoRA models based on established character designs to eliminate style drift.
- Oversee rendering parameters, upscale workflows, and temporal consistency across high-octane 21-minute episodes.

Your Equity:
This is a founding partner role. We operate on a pure capital-efficiency model: you will be contracted for a lifetime 5% Net Profit Share of the entire franchise (including YouTube AdSense, TikTok Creator Rewards, syndication, and merchandise). When the series hits our milestone targets, your equity scales directly with our global market share.

Apply with your portfolio showing multi-shot AI video consistency and custom pipeline workflows. Let’s change the industry.

Job Description:

Chef de la Planification Budgétaire et de la Gouvernance / Head of Business Planning & Governance

***English job description follows***

Description de l'emploi :

Vous avez une expérience en gestion de programme/projet, vous souhaitez travailler dans l’environnement du service à la clientèle au sein d’une équipe dynamique et vous souhaitez évoluer et développer de nouvelles compétences? Ce poste est pour vous !

Le programme d'avions commerciaux A220 recherche un Chef de la Planification Budgétaire et de la Gouvernance pour rejoindre notre équipe Efficacité de la Flotte en service basée à Mirabel (Québec, Canada), où vous travaillerez conjointement avec toute l’organisation de Service à la Clientèle pour supporter les opérateurs A220.

Vous ferez partie de l’équipe Efficacité de la Flotte qui est chargée d’assurer une exploitation sûre et économique de la flotte A220 en service. L'organisation de l'équipe est établie de manière à promouvoir la collaboration transversale de manière autonome, en se soutenant mutuellement et en apprenant collectivement.

Relevant du Chef Efficacité de la flotte en service A220, vous contribuerez à la mission fondamentale de l'équipe qui consiste à garantir une exploitation efficace, sûre et économique de la flotte Airbus A220 en service, tout en améliorant en permanence la satisfaction des clients.

Vous travaillerez sur la gestion de la gouvernance des services clients A220 et soutiendrez précisément la performance de la résolution des principaux problèmes en service de la flotte A220.

Votre environnement de travail:

Le siège du programme d'avions commerciaux A220 est situé à Mirabel, dans la région métropolitaine de Montréal, à deux pas de la ville dynamique de Montréal. Réputée pour son environnement paisible et sûr, la région offre une grande qualité de vie aux jeunes professionnels ou aux professionnels expérimentés, ainsi qu'aux familles, en équilibrant parfaitement les opportunités de carrière et les activités de plein air, ce qui en fait un endroit vraiment spécial où il fait bon vivre.

Parce que nous prenons soin de vous :

Avantages financiers: Salaire attractif, bonus annuel, régime d’assurances collectives, régime de retraite et régime d’achat d’actions.
Équilibre vie privée / professionnelle: Une politique de travail hybride, une cafétéria sur site, une politique de congés très concurrentielle.
Bien-être / santé: Programme d’Aide aux Employé.e.s (PAE), programme de rabais et service médical sur site.
Développement individuel: des opportunités d’évolution et des possibilités de formations nombreuses (catalogue de plus de 10.000 e-formations disponibles en libre accès pour développer votre employabilité, certifications, programmes de développement accéléré, mobilité nationale et internationale).

Chez Airbus, nous vous aidons à travailler, à vous connecter et à collaborer plus facilement et de manière plus flexible. Partout où cela est possible, nous favorisons la flexibilité dans nos modes de travail afin de stimuler l'esprit d'innovation.

Vos défis:

Piloter la performance opérationnelle et économique de l’équipe Efficacité de la Flotte en service et la gouvernance globale de l'organisation Services à la Clientèle A220 en menant les activités transverses suivantes :
Diriger les instances majeures de gouvernance :
Gouvernance MISP / SISP (Major / Significant In-Service Problems) : Assurer le pilotage de la performance de résolution des problèmes majeurs en service, le suivi du calendrier, la gestion des risques et des coûts, la coordination transversale avec l’Ingénierie et les Opérations en service, et la visibilité mensuelle aux clients avec escalade si nécessaire jusqu'au comité exécutif
Comité d'Arbitrage et de Décision du Portefeuille “Amélioration de la satisfaction client” : Structurer et animer la gouvernance d'arbitrage budgétaire et de sélection des projets (validation des business cases, ROI flotte, critères de sévérité, arbitrages et capacité d'exécution).

Coordonner la définition des indicateurs de performance (KPI) pour l'ensemble de l'organisation Services à la Clientèle A220 et garantir leur parfait alignement avec les Top Objectifs Compagnie (TCO/TFO) A220.
Consolider, analyser et rapporter les performances mensuelles de l'entité, et intégrer ces données dans les plateformes de suivi Airbus pour assurer une visibilité transverse complète entre les différents programmes.
Coordonner la sécurité et la navigabilité de la flotte en service en monitorant les campagnes d'actions de modification et d'amélioration en cours d'exécution.
Optimiser les processus internes de gouvernance, garantir l'adhérence aux standards de l'entreprise et déployer la démarche d'Excellence Opérationnelle.
Préparer l'avenir en pilotant la stratégie de transformation, d'évolution du portefeuille de projets transverses et de régionalisation de l'équipe en soutien direct de la proximité client.

Superviser la planification financière globale (AOP - Annual Operating Plan), la gestion du compte de résultat (ABS P&L) et la gestion des risques et opportunités pour l'ensemble des Services à la Clientèle A220.
Gérer les business cases, le suivi des dépenses et les provisions budgétaires des campagnes majeures de modification d'avions (Aircraft Retrofit), représentant un budget de plusieurs dizaines de millions de dollars
Assumer le rôle de responsable du portefeuille (Portfolio Leader) de projets d'amélioration de la satisfaction client, avec la responsabilité complète de l'enveloppe budgétaire annuelle et des arbitrages stratégiques.
Développer la maturité en gestion de projet au sein de l’équipe Efficacité de la Flotte en service, incluant le déploiement de méthodologies, d'outils structurants et de compétences en leadership.

Votre profil:

Diplôme en ingénierie ou gestion de projet;
Minimum de quinze (15) ans d'expérience dans l'ingénierie, l'exploitation d'aéronefs ou la gestion de programmes, avec un minimum de cinq (5) ans dans un rôle de gestion;
Démontre de solides compétences en gestion de projet/programme, y compris en approche agile;
Solide sens financier spécifique à Airbus Canada et expérience souhaitable dans la gestion d'importants projets multidisciplinaires et de budgets à forte valeur;
Excellentes compétences interpersonnelles, de présentation et de communication pour interagir à tous les niveaux de la direction, y compris la capacité à faire des présentations aux cadres supérieurs (Executives) et aux clients;
Est à l'aise dans des écosystèmes complexes et a une compréhension des organisations axées sur la gestion de programmes;
Est orienté(e) processus et a de l'expérience dans l'intégration de nouvelles méthodes de travail;
Promeut le travail d'équipe et agit avec leadership;
Est axé sur le client et fait preuve d'intégrité en tout temps, sans compromis;
Fait preuve d'innovation, d'engagement et de persévérance;
Une expérience en Airbus et/ou A220 et/ou en services à la clientèle est un atout certain.

Passion | Respect | Integrity | Commitment | Innovation.

The Mandate

In a context of sustained growth and transformation of its activities, Lacroix Medical Group is seeking a Director of Information Technology who will actively contribute to the organization's technological evolution.

Reporting directly to the President and CEO, the Director of IT plays a strategic role across the entire network. They are responsible for defining, structuring, and developing the IT function to effectively support the organization's operations, growth, and ambitions.

About the role

Cinareo is hiring a Vice President, Technology: a hands-on technical leader who will own our platform, lead our engineering team and drive our AI roadmap through a period of rapid growth. This role is designed to grow into Chief Technology Officer as Cinareo scales.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will lead, mentor and coordinate the engineers who build our platform, set the technical direction that carries the company through its next stage, and own the results: what we ship, how well it works and how quickly we deliver.

What you will do

First 90 days

Take full ownership of the platform, cloud infrastructure, release process and engineering roadmap from our current engineering lead.
Learn our customers, integrations and data model well enough to make architecture decisions with confidence.
Assess our delivery, quality, security and reliability practices, and set out a plan to strengthen them.

Technical leadership

Architecture and technical direction.
Be the final technical decision-maker on platform architecture, data design and infrastructure. Review designs and critical changes, set engineering standards, and step into the code yourself when a problem calls for it.
Delivery and quality.
Own the release process, test strategy and defect management so we ship predictably and safely.
Reliability and IT operations.
Own uptime, monitoring, incident response and disaster recovery, along with internal IT, identity and access, and device management.
Security and compliance.
Own our compliance program. We hold SOC 1 Type 1 and are completing our SOC 2 Type 2 examination. Maintain control evidence and handle enterprise security reviews accurately and quickly.
Customer and commercial support.
Act as the senior technical counterpart in enterprise sales, partner conversations, onboarding, integration scoping and escalations.

People and team

Lead our distributed engineering team.
Manage, mentor and coordinate a team of full-time and contract engineers across time zones, including off-shore, with clear priorities, deliverables and accountability.
Build the team as we grow.
Decide when to hire, contract or partner; recruit strong engineers; and develop our first technical leads.
Set the culture.
Build an engineering culture grounded in intellectual honesty, ownership and close collaboration with product and design.

AI and growth

AI roadmap.
Lead delivery of our AI roadmap, from AI Assist through Intelligence and Predictive Optimization. This includes the data foundations, LLM and machine-learning capabilities, and the responsible-AI governance enterprise buyers expect.
AI-native engineering.
Make AI part of how we build, using AI-assisted development, testing and operations so a small team can move like a much larger one.
Platform for scale.
Evolve the architecture so reliability, performance and infrastructure cost keep pace as customers and data volumes grow.
Integrations and partnerships.
Own our integration strategy and APIs across CCaaS and WFM and business systems our customers run and support our technology partnerships.
Planning and governance.
Turn the product roadmap into capacity and budget, recommend build, buy or partner decisions, and report technology strategy and risk to the executive team and Board.

How you will work

At first, much of the work is close to the ground: taking ownership of the platform, tightening delivery, quality, reliability and security, and guiding the team through shipping our first AI capabilities. As the team grows and operations run through process and people, the balance shifts toward strategy, the AI roadmap and scaling the organization, and toward the CTO role.

We need someone who moves easily between strategy and execution: working through a production incident with the team in the morning and presenting the technology roadmap to the Executive and the Board in the afternoon, making sound calls with incomplete information, and adjusting quickly as the business scales.

What success looks like

In 6 months:
you own the platform end-to-end, releases are predictable, our AI Assist has shipped, and our SOC 2 Type 2 report is complete.
In 12 months:
the team has clear technical leadership in place, the next phases of our AI roadmap are in delivery, and the platform is ready for the customer growth and technical due diligence that comes with our next stage.

What you bring

10+ years in software engineering, including senior technical leadership at a B2B SaaS company.
A former developer with a strong engineering foundation: you know how to write code, can review it with authority, and earn the respect of the engineers you lead.
A track record of owning delivery outcomes, being accountable for what a team ships, how reliably it runs and whether it lands on time.
Experience shipping AI capabilities, such as LLM-based features, machine learning or both, into a production SaaS product.
Experience designing or evolving cloud SaaS architecture (multi-tenant ideally), including cost and performance management.
Experience leading and mentoring distributed teams, including contractors or partner teams both on-shore and off-shore, and hiring and developing engineers.
Credibility with enterprise customers and partners on architecture, security and integration.
Clear written communication that executives and Board members can act on.
Real enthusiasm for AI and how it is changing both software products and the way software gets built.

Nice to have

Contact center technology: WFM and CCaaS (Genesys, Aspect, Verint, NICE, Five9, Amazon Connect or similar)
Leading a security compliance program (SOC 2, ISO 27001 or equivalent) at the level of controls and evidence.
Calculation-heavy domains such as forecasting, simulation or optimization.
Responsible-AI governance.

Career path:
Designed to grow into Chief Technology Officer

Remote. Ontario preferred, but must be based in Canada

Commensurate with experience

with a short note covering:
a SaaS platform or engineering team you scaled, and how you led the team that built it; and

Strong understanding of governance, security, privacy, technology risk, operational resilience and support models in a regulated environment
Ability to translate emerging technology into practical employee and business value
Strong communication, influencing, stakeholder-management and decision-framing skills
Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary work, manage priorities and coordinate delivery across organizational boundaries
Collaborative, pragmatic, change-oriented and outcome-focused leadership style

About the role

Cinareo is hiring a Vice President, Technology: a hands-on technical leader who will own our platform, lead our engineering team and drive our AI roadmap through a period of rapid growth. This role is designed to grow into Chief Technology Officer as Cinareo scales.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will lead, mentor and coordinate the engineers who build our platform, set the technical direction that carries the company through its next stage, and own the results: what we ship, how well it works and how quickly we deliver.

What you will do

First 90 days

Take full ownership of the platform, cloud infrastructure, release process and engineering roadmap from our current engineering lead.
Learn our customers, integrations and data model well enough to make architecture decisions with confidence.
Assess our delivery, quality, security and reliability practices, and set out a plan to strengthen them.

Technical leadership

Architecture and technical direction.
Be the final technical decision-maker on platform architecture, data design and infrastructure. Review designs and critical changes, set engineering standards, and step into the code yourself when a problem calls for it.
Delivery and quality.
Own the release process, test strategy and defect management so we ship predictably and safely.
Reliability and IT operations.
Own uptime, monitoring, incident response and disaster recovery, along with internal IT, identity and access, and device management.
Security and compliance.
Own our compliance program. We hold SOC 1 Type 1 and are completing our SOC 2 Type 2 examination. Maintain control evidence and handle enterprise security reviews accurately and quickly.
Customer and commercial support.
Act as the senior technical counterpart in enterprise sales, partner conversations, onboarding, integration scoping and escalations.

People and team

Lead our distributed engineering team.
Manage, mentor and coordinate a team of full-time and contract engineers across time zones, including off-shore, with clear priorities, deliverables and accountability.
Build the team as we grow.
Decide when to hire, contract or partner; recruit strong engineers; and develop our first technical leads.
Set the culture.
Build an engineering culture grounded in intellectual honesty, ownership and close collaboration with product and design.

AI and growth

AI roadmap.
Lead delivery of our AI roadmap, from AI Assist through Intelligence and Predictive Optimization. This includes the data foundations, LLM and machine-learning capabilities, and the responsible-AI governance enterprise buyers expect.
AI-native engineering.
Make AI part of how we build, using AI-assisted development, testing and operations so a small team can move like a much larger one.
Platform for scale.
Evolve the architecture so reliability, performance and infrastructure cost keep pace as customers and data volumes grow.
Integrations and partnerships.
Own our integration strategy and APIs across CCaaS and WFM and business systems our customers run and support our technology partnerships.
Planning and governance.
Turn the product roadmap into capacity and budget, recommend build, buy or partner decisions, and report technology strategy and risk to the executive team and Board.

How you will work

At first, much of the work is close to the ground: taking ownership of the platform, tightening delivery, quality, reliability and security, and guiding the team through shipping our first AI capabilities. As the team grows and operations run through process and people, the balance shifts toward strategy, the AI roadmap and scaling the organization, and toward the CTO role.

We need someone who moves easily between strategy and execution: working through a production incident with the team in the morning and presenting the technology roadmap to the Executive and the Board in the afternoon, making sound calls with incomplete information, and adjusting quickly as the business scales.

What success looks like

In 6 months:
you own the platform end-to-end, releases are predictable, our AI Assist has shipped, and our SOC 2 Type 2 report is complete.
In 12 months:
the team has clear technical leadership in place, the next phases of our AI roadmap are in delivery, and the platform is ready for the customer growth and technical due diligence that comes with our next stage.

What you bring

10+ years in software engineering, including senior technical leadership at a B2B SaaS company.
A former developer with a strong engineering foundation: you know how to write code, can review it with authority, and earn the respect of the engineers you lead.
A track record of owning delivery outcomes, being accountable for what a team ships, how reliably it runs and whether it lands on time.
Experience shipping AI capabilities, such as LLM-based features, machine learning or both, into a production SaaS product.
Experience designing or evolving cloud SaaS architecture (multi-tenant ideally), including cost and performance management.
Experience leading and mentoring distributed teams, including contractors or partner teams both on-shore and off-shore, and hiring and developing engineers.
Credibility with enterprise customers and partners on architecture, security and integration.
Clear written communication that executives and Board members can act on.
Real enthusiasm for AI and how it is changing both software products and the way software gets built.

Nice to have

Contact center technology: WFM and CCaaS (Genesys, Aspect, Verint, NICE, Five9, Amazon Connect or similar)
Leading a security compliance program (SOC 2, ISO 27001 or equivalent) at the level of controls and evidence.
Calculation-heavy domains such as forecasting, simulation or optimization.
Responsible-AI governance.

Details

Reports to:
Chief Operating Officer
Career path:
Designed to grow into Chief Technology Officer
Location:
Remote. Ontario preferred, but must be based in Canada
Compensation:
Commensurate with experience

To apply

Send your CV to hr@cinareo.com
with a short note covering:
a SaaS platform or engineering team you scaled, and how you led the team that built it; and
your experience with AI and where you see it making the biggest difference in the dev-ops and our production platform.

new_jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

Anthropic Fellows Program Overview

The Anthropic Fellows Program is designed to foster AI research and engineering talent. We provide funding and mentorship to promising technical talent - regardless of previous experience.

Fellows will primarily use external infrastructure (e.g. open-source models, public APIs) to work on project aligned with our research priorities, with the goal of producing a public output
(e.g. a paper submission). In one of our earlier cohorts, over 80% of fellows produced papers. We run multiple cohorts of Fellows each year and review applications on a rolling basis.

Submit your application to the Economics & Policy workstream at the bottom of this page. We are accepting applications on a rolling basis for the next cohort expected to start in January 2027. In some circumstances, we can accommodate fellows starting outside the usual cohort timelines — please note in your application if the January 2027 start date doesn't work for you.

What To Expect

4 months of full-time research
Direct mentorship from Anthropic researchers
Weekly stipend of 3,850 USD / 2,310 GBP / 4,300 CAD + benefits (these vary by country)
Substantial funding for compute and other research expenses

Interview process

The interview process will include an initial application, assessments, and interviews. We may ask for references later in the process as well.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Compensation

The expected base stipend for this role is 3,850 USD / 2,310 GBP / 4,300 CAD per week, with an expectation of 40 hours per week for 4 months (with possible extension).

The Anthropic Institute Fellows (Economics & Policy)

Mentors, research areas, & past projects

Fellows will undergo a project selection & mentor matching process. Potential research areas and mentors include:

Economics
Maxim Massenkoff
Peter McCrory

Policy, Security, and Society
Jack Clark
Marina Favaro
Jim Baker

Projects In This Workstream May Include

Designing and conducting empirical research on AI's economic effects, drawing on external data sources
Developing new methodological approaches for studying AI's impact on labor markets, the future of work, and society
Analysing the offense–defense balance for AI-enabled cyber and bio capabilities as models scale
Measuring the extent to which model performance increases with custom harnesses
Identifying market driven mechanisms that could improve societal resilience to anticipated threats from AI systems
Identifying which metrics relating to AI R&D could serve as early warning signals for recursive self-improvement

For Past Project Examples, See

How AI Impacts Skill Formation: Judy Shen and Alex Tamkin
Stress-Testing Model Specs Reveals Character Differences among Language Models: Jifan Zhang, Henry Sleight, Andi Peng, John Schulman, and Esin Durmus

Unique candidate criteria

You might be a particularly great fit for this workstream if you:

Have an interest in economics or policy research; prior experience in this area is a plus but not required
Are adaptable and collaborative, able to take direction and contribute to team priorities rather than needing to pursue a predetermined research agenda
Are skilled at writing up and communicating your results, even when they're null or unexpected
Are passionate about translating research insights into actionable recommendations for improving AI systems and informing policy

You May Be a Good Fit If You

Are motivated by making sure AI is safe and beneficial for society as a whole
Are excited to transition into AI research and would be interested in a full-time role at Anthropic
Strong track record of empirical research
Thrive in fast-paced, collaborative environments
Can implement ideas quickly and communicate clearly

Candidates Must Be

Fluent in Python programming
Available to work full-time on the Fellows program

Logistics - Fellows Program

Submit your application to the Anthropic Institute Fellows at the bottom of this page.

Logistics Requirements:
To participate in the Fellows program, you must have work authorization in the US, UK, or Canada and be located in that country during the program.

Workspace Locations:
We have designated shared workspaces in SF. We are also open to remote fellows in the UK, US, or Canada
.

Visa Sponsorship:
We are not
currently able to sponsor visas for fellows. To participate in the Fellows program, you need to have or independently obtain full-time work authorization in the UK, the US, or Canada.

Program Duration:
The program runs for 4 months, full-time. If you can't commit to the full duration, please still apply and note your constraints in the application. We review these requests on a case-by-case basis.

The below are Anthropic's policies for full time roles. These do NOT apply to the Fellows Program.

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues.
